title: Last work with Bill Boyd before the Army in 1942
summary: Parker kept playing with the country bands until about 1942, when he entered the Army. In 1945 he went to Los Angeles and left that scene for good.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: They gotta write down and tell him about it. We're waiting. Uh, you, you stopped playing with the Cotterians. You stopped playing with the country bands in about what year?

Oh, right up to when I joined the, uh, my last day with the, with the, uh, Bill Boyd must have been in, as late as, uh, 42, right before we're in the Army, I think. Real late. When I left to go to the Army, that was the end of all that, but as long as I was around in Fort Worth, and as long as they were recording, I was there. When did you come out of the Army? In 45, in Los Angeles. Oh. No, no. In 45 we took right off for Los Angeles. At once. Then left the scene entirely, forever. Never to go back again. And it wasn't the, it couldn't have been the same any time.
